description: The MA in African American & Black Diaspora Studies provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the historical, social, political, economic, and cultural experiences of people of African descent in the United States and across the diaspora. Our curriculum is designed to deepen students’ knowledge of the foundational texts, theories, and methodologies of the field, while also encouraging them to explore emerging scholarship and critical debates. Students will develop advanced research, analytical, and communication skills, preparing them for doctoral study in African American Studies or related fields, as well as for careers in education, public policy, community advocacy, and the arts.
Program name: Master of Arts in African American & Black Diaspora Studies

Concentration name: African American and Black Diaspora Studies PhD Track
description: Students applying for doctoral work in American Studies who wish to concentrate their studies on African American and Black Diaspora Studies should indicate this on their application. The African American and Black Diaspora Studies Track (AABD) provides students with an interdisciplinary program of study and training in critical theories and methods. This track introduces students to the complex histories, cultures, and politics of people of African descent, with a particular focus on the experiences of African Americans, Afro-Caribbean, and Black diasporic communities in the Americas. The AABD track provides students with the critical and historical tools needed to understand Black life in a national and transnational context, and to address social, political, and cultural challenges with theoretical sophistication and methodological rigor. Students in the AABD track complete all requirements of the American Studies PhD, but structure their coursework, language examination, qualifying examination, and dissertation toward the AABD track.
Program name: PhD in African American & Black Diaspora Studies

description: The MA in American Studies offers students an opportunity to study American culture and society from an interdisciplinary perspective. We offer a holistic program that integrates approaches from fields ranging from literary studies, history, and sociology, to art history, religious studies, and music. The MA is a valuable terminal degree, offering an excellent foundation for professional work in fields ranging from journalism, law, public policy, and business to museum and archival studies, library sciences, and teaching. It also serves as an excellent stepping stone for students who wish to go on to pursue doctoral work in American Studies or related fields.
Program name: Master of Arts in American Studies

description: The Boston University American Studies Program offers a PhD in American Studies. The program draws on faculty and students from across the humanities and social sciences, providing students with an opportunity to work in several fields while also developing a particular specialization. The American Studies Program trains students in an interdisciplinary approach to the study of American cultures and societies. We invite students to define their own areas of inquiry, drawing on the resources of the entire university. In recent years, our students have pursued topics ranging from the global dimensions of American music and empire, to the politics of race and reproduction in the nineteenth century, to the role of museums in shaping public memory, to the transformation of American landscape and environmental consciousness, to histories of sexuality, performance, and the body in the twentieth century. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in higher education and related fields.
Program name: PhD in American Studies

description: Preservation Studies at Boston University prepares students for careers in historic preservation with a flexible, interdisciplinary program offered through the American & New England Studies Program (AMES). Our location in Boston, a city with a rich history and a leader in preservation, provides students with unmatched access to historical sites, public agencies, and private organizations. The program’s rigorous curriculum provides a strong academic grounding in the history, theory, and practice of historic preservation while our many internship opportunities provide valuable practical experience. The Master of Arts in Preservation Studies (MA PS) is designed for students interested in preparing for professional positions in historic preservation or pursuing further graduate study. It is an interdisciplinary program housed in the American & New England Studies Program in the College of Arts & Sciences. The MA PS curriculum combines a strong academic grounding in the history, theory, and practice of historic preservation with opportunities for practical experience and exposure to various aspects of the field. Students benefit from the program’s small size, the expertise of its faculty, the wealth of resources available in Boston and New England, and the opportunity to engage with a vast network of alumni and preservation professionals.
Program name: Master of Arts in Preservation Studies

description: The dual Master of Arts (MA) in Preservation Studies and Juris Doctor (JD) degree offered by Boston University’s Graduate School of Arts & Sciences and School of Law, respectively, is designed for students who plan to pursue careers as preservationists, land use planners, or attorneys specializing in historic preservation, cultural heritage law, or real estate development. This unique program allows students to delve into the historical, theoretical, and practical aspects of preservation, while simultaneously gaining a thorough understanding of the legal frameworks that govern it. The curriculum integrates coursework from both disciplines, providing students with a comprehensive skill set to address the complex challenges of urban planning, environmental stewardship, and cultural resource management. Graduates of the MA/JD program will be equipped to work in various settings, including government agencies, non-profit organizations, law firms, and private consulting practices, where they can advocate for and implement effective preservation strategies.
Program name: Master of Arts / Juris Doctor in Preservation Studies

description: The Department of Anthropology offers an MA in Anthropology for students interested in advanced interdisciplinary study, as well as those pursuing the MA as part of a doctoral program. The program is designed to provide students with a strong theoretical foundation across the subfields of sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, and biological anthropology, as well as rigorous training in research design, methodology, and analysis. Students are prepared for a range of professional opportunities in academia and in the private and public sectors, locally and internationally.
Program name: Master of Arts in Anthropology

description: The PhD program in Anthropology provides students with the training needed to become successful scholars and researchers in anthropological subfields including sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. Our program emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches, rigorous methodological training, and a commitment to fieldwork and empirical research. Students benefit from close mentorship by faculty, access to cutting-edge research facilities, and opportunities for fieldwork both locally and internationally. Graduates of our program are prepared for careers in academia, museums, NGOs, and government agencies, among other sectors. We encourage prospective students to explore the research interests of our faculty members to identify potential mentors.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology

description: The MA in Public Anthropology at Boston University provides students with a strong foundation in anthropological theory and practice. Combining coursework in sociocultural anthropology with hands-on training, the MA program emphasizes the study of contemporary global issues and engaged research practices. This program equips students with the skills to address pressing social concerns, engage diverse publics, and apply anthropological insights in various professional settings, including non-profits, government agencies, cultural institutions, and research organizations.
Program name: Master of Arts in Public Anthropology

description: The MA program in Archaeology at Boston University is a two-year degree designed to provide students with a strong foundation in archaeological theory and method, as well as the ability to specialize in particular archaeological fields. Many of our MA students use the degree as preparation for doctoral studies; others use it to launch careers in cultural resource management or other archaeological endeavors. The MA in Archaeology is designed for students seeking either to deepen their knowledge of the field prior to applying for a PhD program or to acquire the training necessary for a professional career in archaeology. Students are expected to complete 32 credits (8 courses) and an MA thesis or two qualifying papers. Students are encouraged to pursue an archaeological field school and participate in departmental research projects. Students typically fulfill their requirements over two academic years.
Program name: Master of Arts in Archaeology

description: The PhD program in Archaeology is designed for students interested in advanced scholarly training and research. Students may concentrate in a wide variety of geographical and temporal areas, theoretical approaches, and methodological specialties, limited only by the particular interests of the faculty. The PhD program provides students with the advanced skills and knowledge needed to pursue academic careers and leadership positions in cultural resource management, museum studies, and other related fields. Students gain expertise in archaeological theory, method, and practice, and develop strong research and writing skills through coursework, fieldwork, and dissertation research. They will learn how to: Develop and conduct original archaeological research. Analyze and interpret archaeological data. Communicate research findings effectively through written and oral presentations. Teach archaeology at the university level. Contribute to the preservation and management of cultural heritage.
Program name: PhD in Archaeology

description: The MA in Archaeological & Environmental Sciences (MA AES) is an intensive, 12-month interdisciplinary program designed to train students in the application of scientific methods to the study of archaeological questions. The program emphasizes the practical experience of designing and conducting research, analyzing scientific data in the laboratory, and engaging in field-based data collection. Students learn how to analyze the chemical, physical, and biological properties of archaeological materials and their associated environments. Training occurs in the department’s state-of-the-art laboratories and through ongoing field projects in archaeology. This program prepares students for careers in cultural resource management, museums, archaeological field research, scientific laboratories, and provides a strong foundation for doctoral work in archaeology or related fields.
Program name: Master of Arts in Archaeological & Environmental Sciences/Archaeology

description: The MA in Classics & Archaeology at Boston University combines the study of Greek and Latin languages and literatures with the theory and practice of classical archaeology. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in classical antiquity, preparing them for further graduate study at the PhD level or for careers in related fields such as museum work, cultural heritage management, or education. Students gain a deep understanding of the classical world through rigorous coursework, research opportunities, and engagement with archaeological fieldwork. The program encourages interdisciplinary approaches and offers flexibility for students to tailor their studies to their interests within the broad scope of Classics and Archaeology.
Program name: Master of Arts in Classics & Archaeology

description: The MA program in Astronomy at Boston University’s Graduate School of Arts & Sciences provides students with a solid understanding of the physical processes governing the universe, preparing them for careers in science, industry, and education. Graduates are well-prepared for entry into PhD programs in astronomy and related fields, or for positions in industry or secondary education. They will have a strong foundation in astrophysics, as well as a range of skills in computation, data analysis, and scientific communication. Our MA students engage in research in a variety of areas of astronomy including planetary science, exoplanets, stellar astrophysics, galactic and extragalactic astronomy, cosmology, and instrumentation. Faculty research programs focus on theoretical, observational, and experimental investigations. MA students can participate in several research projects during their time at BU, developing expertise across a broad range of subjects.
Program name: Master of Arts in Astronomy

description: The Department of Astronomy offers an exceptional learning experience, coupling a dynamic, intellectually stimulating, and collaborative environment with world-class facilities and research opportunities. Our doctoral program trains students to become scientific leaders in academia, government, and industry through a curriculum that emphasizes a combination of coursework, research experience, and professional development. We provide ample opportunities to grow intellectually by offering the chance to interact with a vibrant community of faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and graduate students who are at the forefront of astronomical research. We have expertise in diverse research areas, including Planetary Science, Exoplanets, Solar and Space Physics, Galaxies, Quasars, and Cosmology, and Interstellar Medium and Star Formation. We expect our students to contribute to the field by producing original research, publish their findings in peer-reviewed journals, and present their work at scientific conferences. Students will also gain valuable experience and training in teaching as part of their academic development.
Program name: PhD in Astronomy

description: The Master of Arts in Astronomy (Astrophysics & Space Physics) provides students with a strong foundation in astrophysics, space physics, and instrumentation. Graduates will be prepared to pursue doctoral studies in astrophysics or space physics, or for careers in related fields. Students in the MA in Astronomy (Astrophysics & Space Physics) program are required to take eight courses (32 credits). Students will be advised by a faculty member in the Department of Astronomy and will tailor a course of study to their individual interests and goals. Possible courses include computational physics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, stellar atmospheres and interiors, galaxies and cosmology, and space plasma physics. Students will also participate in research with a faculty member, culminating in a Master’s thesis or project in astrophysics or space physics.
Program name: Master of Arts in Astrophysics & Space Physics

Concentration name: Cell and Molecular Biology, Ecology, Behavior and Evolution, Marine Biology, Neuroscience
description: The Master of Science (MS) program in Biology is designed for students who wish to deepen their understanding of biology through advanced coursework and research. The program provides a broad education in biology with opportunities for specialization in areas such as cell and molecular biology, ecology, behavior and evolution, marine biology, and neuroscience. Students develop critical thinking, laboratory, and research skills, preparing them for careers in research, education, biotechnology, or further graduate studies.
Program name: Master of Science in Biology

description: The PhD in Biology program is designed to provide students with the depth and breadth of knowledge necessary to excel in the biological sciences. Our students undertake cutting-edge research under the mentorship of faculty who are leaders in their fields, developing the skills and expertise needed for successful careers in academia, industry, government, and non-profit organizations. The program fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, preparing graduates to address complex biological challenges and contribute to scientific discovery.
Program name: PhD in Biology

description: Boston University’s MS in Biostatistics program is located in the Department of Biostatistics, which is part of the School of Public Health (SPH). The program is a collaboration between SPH and the Graduate Medical Sciences (GMS) departments, allowing students to access a diverse range of faculty and resources. The program’s curriculum provides students with a solid foundation in biostatistical theory and methods, as well as practical experience in applying these methods to real-world problems. Graduates are prepared for careers in research, public health, and industry, or for further graduate studies. Our mission is to train students in the theory and application of biostatistics, preparing them for successful careers in academia, industry, and government. We emphasize critical thinking, problem-solving, and effective communication skills.
Program name: Master of Science in Biostatistics

description: Biostatistics is an indispensable tool in biomedical research. It provides the quantitative and analytical methods used to draw sound conclusions from scientific data. As a PhD student in Biostatistics, you will develop a solid theoretical background in statistical inference and probability, and apply that knowledge to the design and analysis of biomedical and public health studies. You will conduct original methodological research, participate in collaborative research projects, and become well-versed in statistical computing and programming. PhD students receive a thorough grounding in biostatistical theory and methods in a challenging environment that emphasizes statistical application and collaboration. A typical program takes five years to complete. Coursework is balanced between theoretical foundations and applied methods, with an emphasis on development of original research skills. Through coursework, collaborative research with faculty, and dissertation research, students develop expertise in a wide range of biostatistical methods. Throughout your time in the program, you will deepen your expertise in statistical computing, data analysis, and the presentation of statistical findings. You will engage in discussions with faculty and students about the role of biostatistics in biomedical research, and participate in ongoing research projects. These experiences will prepare you for a successful career as an independent biostatistical researcher.
Program name: PhD in Biostatistics
Master of Arts in Biotechnology
Master of Science in Biotechnology

description: The MA in Chemistry program is designed to enhance the knowledge and skills of individuals with a bachelor’s degree in chemistry or a closely related field. It provides students with advanced coursework and research experience in various areas of chemistry, including analytical, inorganic, organic, physical, and biochemistry. The program prepares graduates for careers in research and development, teaching, or further graduate studies in chemistry or related fields.
Program name: Master of Arts in Chemistry

description: Boston University’s Chemistry Department offers a PhD in Chemistry degree program focusing on a diverse range of research areas, including inorganic, organic, physical, and theoretical chemistry, as well as analytical chemistry, materials chemistry, and chemical biology. The PhD program is tailored to students’ individual needs and interests, providing them with the flexibility to design a course of study that aligns with their goals. Students will take courses in advanced chemistry topics and conduct original research under the guidance of a faculty mentor. The program culminates in the completion and defense of a doctoral dissertation. Graduates of the PhD in Chemistry program are well-prepared for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can apply their expertise to address complex scientific challenges.
Program name: PhD in Chemistry

Concentration name: Track A: Ancient History and Classical Archaeology; Track B: Ancient Languages and Literatures
description: The MA in Classical Studies at Boston University’s Department of Classical Studies offers students the opportunity to pursue advanced study of ancient Greek and Roman culture. Our program provides a rigorous course of study in preparation for PhD programs in Classics and related fields, as well as for careers in education, libraries, museums, and other areas where a background in the humanities is valued. Students are encouraged to develop a broad understanding of the field, while also specializing in particular areas through their choice of courses and thesis topic. The MA can be pursued on a full- or part-time basis. Full-time students typically complete the degree in 3 semesters (1.5 years). Part-time students typically complete the degree in 2–3 years. The MA in Classical Studies has two distinct tracks: Track A, focusing on ancient history and classical archaeology, and Track B, focusing on ancient languages and literatures.
Program name: Master of Arts in Classical Studies

description: The PhD program in Classical Studies offers advanced training in the literatures, cultures, and history of ancient Greece and Rome. Students gain comprehensive knowledge of Greek and Latin language and literature through coursework, qualifying examinations, and dissertation research. The program enables students to achieve professional expertise in the field and prepares them for careers as college and university teachers and scholars.
Program name: PhD in Classical Studies

description: The MFA program in Literary Translation provides a balance of theoretical and practical work in the translation of texts from ancient or modern languages into English. It encourages students to cultivate competence in the literary, linguistic, and cultural traditions of their chosen languages, and to acquire advanced skill in English prose style and versification. Students may specialize in the translation of literary texts from a wide array of ancient or modern languages. Upon graduation, students are prepared to undertake professional translation or to pursue further graduate work in comparative literature or related fields.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Ancient Greek/Literary Translation

description: The joint MA/PhD program in Classical Studies and Philosophy at Boston University is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students grounding in both fields while encouraging them to bridge the traditional gap between them. Students are introduced to issues in ancient philosophy and classics from the beginning of their graduate careers. This unique collaboration provides an exceptional opportunity to study the ancient world in an interdisciplinary context. The program combines the individual strengths of the Classical Studies department and the Philosophy department at Boston University, both of which have significant reputations in ancient philosophy. The Classical Studies department’s particular strengths in Greek and Latin literature, ancient history, and archaeology complement the Philosophy department’s strengths across the history of philosophy and contemporary philosophical fields. Faculty from both departments jointly advise students in the program.
Program name: Master of Arts / Doctor of Philosophy in Classical Studies/Philosophy

description: The Boston University MFA in Literary Translation is a two-year degree for committed, advanced students of literary translation. We seek highly capable individuals who can demonstrate a strong command of their source and target languages and a significant interest in the art and craft of literary translation. The goal of the program is to educate students in the practical and theoretical challenges inherent in literary translation, and to provide the tools necessary for beginning a career as a professional literary translator. The program culminates in a critical introduction to and full translation of a book-length work suitable for publication. Graduates will leave with a strong sense of their own emerging professional voice as well as a substantial portfolio of publishable material, and will be prepared to embark on a career as an independent literary translator.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Latin/Literary Translation

description: The Master of Arts (MA) program in Cognitive & Neural Systems (CNS) provides students with a strong quantitative and computational background in the foundations of cognitive and neural sciences, preparing them for advanced research in the field. Students learn to apply computational modeling and empirical methods to understand cognitive and neural phenomena. The program is specifically designed to train students for future doctoral work in cognitive and neural systems and related fields. It offers a unique interdisciplinary approach, drawing faculty from across Boston University, including Psychological & Brain Sciences, Computer Science, Biology, Biomedical Engineering, and Philosophy.
Program name: Master of Arts in Cognitive & Neural Systems

description: BU’s PhD in Cognitive & Neural Systems (CNS) brings together researchers and students from a variety of disciplines—including psychology, computer science, linguistics, mathematics, and engineering—to explore fundamental questions about the mind and brain. Through coursework and research, students gain a deep understanding of human and animal cognition and neural systems. The program emphasizes both computational and experimental approaches, with opportunities for students to engage in interdisciplinary research across different departments and centers. Graduates of the CNS PhD program are prepared for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can contribute to advancements in artificial intelligence, neuroscience, and cognitive science.
Program name: PhD in Cognitive & Neural Systems

description: The Master of Science (MS) in Computer Science is a professional degree program intended for students with a bachelor’s degree in computer science or a closely related field. It provides students with both a broad and deep education in computer science and prepares them for further graduate study or for a professional career in computer science.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science

description: The Ph.D. program in Computer Science at Boston University is a research-oriented program designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at universities and in industrial laboratories. Students are expected to complete their degree within five years. The program typically involves two years of coursework, two years of research leading to a dissertation, and one year devoted entirely to dissertation work. Some students may take longer if they enter with a master’s degree and complete more coursework. Students in the Ph.D. program receive financial support, including tuition remission and a stipend for living expenses. For more information, please visit our Financial Support page. Successful Ph.D. graduates go on to careers in academia and industry. Recent graduates have accepted positions at top universities such as Columbia, Cornell, Harvard, Johns Hopkins, NYU, Stanford, UC Berkeley, UIUC, and Yale. Others have joined leading industrial research labs such as Google, IBM, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta. More information about recent graduates can be found on our Alumni page. Please consult the GRS Bulletin for the most up-to-date information on degree requirements and courses.
Program name: PhD in Computer Science

description: Boston University’s MS in Artificial Intelligence (MSAI) is offered through the Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences (CDS) and the Department of Computer Science (CS) in the College of Arts & Sciences. The MS in AI is a STEM-designated professional master’s program designed to equip students with the necessary knowledge and skills to develop and deploy cutting-edge AI systems and to assume leadership roles in the rapidly evolving AI industry. The curriculum covers foundational topics in AI, machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and robotics, as well as ethical considerations and societal impact of AI. The program is designed to be completed in three to four semesters and requires 32 credits beyond the bachelor’s degree.
Program name: Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence

description: The Master of Science (MS) in Computer Science program focuses on the design, analysis, and implementation of computer systems. Graduates are prepared for careers in industry or for further graduate study. The department offers a wide range of courses and research opportunities in computer science, including such areas as artificial intelligence, data mining, database systems, scientific computing, software engineering, theory of computation, networking, operating systems, programming languages and compilers, and security. Full-time students typically complete the program in three to four semesters.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science with Specialization in Cyber Security

description: The Master of Science in Computer Science program is designed for students seeking to deepen their understanding of fundamental computer science principles and to gain advanced skills in specific areas of computing. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, preparing graduates for successful careers in industry, research, or further doctoral studies. Students engage with cutting-edge research through various courses, seminars, and projects, guided by faculty renowned for their contributions to diverse fields such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, cybersecurity, and software engineering. Graduates of the program are well-prepared to tackle complex computational challenges and contribute to advancements in technology.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science with Specialization in Data-Centric Computing

description: Boston University’s MFA program in Creative Writing, founded in 1965 by John Malcolm Brinnin, is a two-year intensive program focused on either poetry or fiction. Students concentrate in one genre, taking workshops and graduate-level literature courses in that genre, with the option to take one workshop in the alternate genre if space permits. Small workshops led by award-winning faculty provide a supportive and challenging environment for writers committed to a literary life, intended for those who wish to write at the highest level of accomplishment and professionalism. Over the course of four semesters, students complete a collection of stories, a novel, or a book-length manuscript of poems. Graduates of the program have published books with major presses, won numerous awards, and gone on to teach creative writing at universities around the country.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing

description:
The Master of Arts (MA) in Earth & Environment provides a rigorous interdisciplinary graduate-level education in Earth and environmental sciences, preparing students for careers in research, government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector, as well as for further doctoral work. Students in the program develop a strong background in Earth science, coupled with breadth in the interdisciplinary field of environmental science. The program builds on the exceptional research strengths of faculty in the Department of Earth & Environment, who conduct cutting-edge research across a wide range of topics, from climate change, oceanography, and biogeoscience to remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), human-environment interactions, and environmental policy.

The MA program is designed to provide maximum flexibility and can be tailored to individual students’ interests through a wide array of course offerings in areas such as biogeoscience, remote sensing/GIS, urban environmental systems, environmental policy and planning, and Earth surface processes. Students have the option to pursue a thesis or a non-thesis track, both of which require a comprehensive examination. Thesis-track students conduct original research and write a master’s thesis, while non-thesis track students develop a research project or professional report that demonstrates their mastery of the field. The program emphasizes both foundational knowledge and the development of strong analytical and communication skills, preparing graduates to tackle complex environmental challenges.
Program name: Master of Arts in Earth & Environment

description: The PhD in Earth & Environment is designed for students interested in advanced studies in Earth and environmental sciences. Students are admitted into a particular research area and typically complete coursework, a qualifying exam, a comprehensive exam, and a dissertation. The program prepares students for careers in academia, government, and industry, or for other positions that require advanced scientific training and research skills. A hallmark of the program is its interdisciplinary approach, drawing on faculty expertise across various fields within the department and beyond. Students are encouraged to pursue research that crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries, addressing complex environmental challenges from multiple perspectives. The program emphasizes both foundational knowledge and cutting-edge research, providing students with the skills and intellectual framework to become independent scholars and leaders in their fields. Students work closely with faculty mentors to develop and execute original research projects, culminating in a significant doctoral dissertation.
Program name: PhD in Earth & Environment

description: The Master of Science (MS) in Earth & Environment program at Boston University offers students advanced training and research opportunities in the Earth, environmental, and planetary sciences. Students gain in-depth understanding of fundamental concepts and develop quantitative and analytical skills applicable to a wide range of careers in environmental consulting, government agencies, NGOs, research, and academia. The program provides a flexible curriculum that allows students to tailor their studies to their interests. Students in the MS in Earth & Environment can specialize in various research areas, including biogeoscience, geochronology and surficial processes, hydrology, oceanography, remote sensing, and paleo-climate. Students interested in the remote sensing and geospatial sciences concentration should apply to the MS in Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences.
Program name: Master of Science in Earth & Environment

description: A 32-credit interdisciplinary program for students with backgrounds in the natural sciences, social sciences, or engineering, the MA in Energy & Environment provides students with the analytical and quantitative skills needed to address the complex challenges posed by changes in the global climate and energy supply. Students develop expertise in the interactions among energy systems, technology, economics, and public policy, and in the scientific and economic dimensions of environmental change. The MA in Energy & Environment is offered jointly by the Department of Earth & Environment and the Department of Economics. Through coursework and research, students in the Energy & Environment program engage with faculty and each other in a highly collaborative environment. Students in the program develop skills in empirical research methods, data analysis, and advanced econometric techniques in preparation for careers in both the public and private sectors. Graduates are well prepared for careers in government, consulting, non-profit organizations, and industry focused on energy, environmental protection, natural resource management, climate change mitigation, and sustainability.
Program name: Master of Science in Energy & Environment

description: The Dual Degree in Energy & Environment (MS) and Business Administration (MBA) provides students with an integrated understanding of environmental science, policy, and law, combined with a strong foundation in business management. This interdisciplinary program is designed for students who want to develop solutions to complex energy and environmental challenges from both a scientific and business perspective. Students gain expertise in areas such as renewable energy, climate change, sustainable development, environmental economics, and corporate social responsibility. The curriculum emphasizes analytical skills, strategic thinking, and practical problem-solving through case studies, projects, and fieldwork. Graduates are prepared for leadership roles in various sectors, including environmental consulting, renewable energy companies, government agencies, non-profit organizations, and corporate sustainability departments.
Program name: Master of Science in Energy & Environment / Master of Business Administration
Master of Science in Environmental Analysis & Policy/Energy & Environment

description: The Energy & Environment concentration of the MS in Earth & Environment provides a rigorous interdisciplinary approach to understanding the scientific, economic, and policy challenges associated with developing a sustainable energy future. Students gain a fundamental understanding of earth systems and the interconnections between energy and the environment while developing advanced knowledge of energy science, technology, economics, and policy. Through coursework, field experiences, and research, students develop the skills to evaluate conventional and renewable energy systems, analyze environmental impacts, and formulate effective solutions for a just energy transition. The curriculum prepares graduates for careers in the energy sector, environmental consulting, government agencies, non-profits, and further graduate study.
Program name: Master of Science in Earth & Environmental Sciences/Energy & Environment

description: Boston University’s Master of Science (MS) program in Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences provides students with a strong theoretical and practical foundation in the analysis and application of remote sensing and geographic information systems (GIS). Graduates of the program are able to critically evaluate state-of-the-art remote sensing and GIS methods and apply these to a wide range of problems in environmental science, urban planning, public health, and business. The program helps students understand: Physical principles of remote sensing Image processing, analysis, and visualization Mathematical and statistical methods for analyzing geographic data Design and implementation of GIS Applications of remote sensing and GIS to address real-world problems
Program name: Master of Science in Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences
Master of Science in Environmental Analysis & Policy/Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences

description: The Master of Science program in Earth & Environmental Sciences with a specialization in Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences (RS & GS) at Boston University focuses on the science and applications of earth observation and geospatial technologies. The program trains students in the theory and application of remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), and global positioning systems (GPS) to study the Earth’s surface and atmosphere. Through a unique interdisciplinary curriculum that combines rigorous coursework with practical, hands-on experience, students gain expertise in analyzing and interpreting large geospatial datasets, developing and implementing geospatial models, and designing and conducting independent research. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in environmental consulting, government agencies, non-profit organizations, and academia, as well as for further graduate study in related fields.
Program name: Master of Science in Earth & Environmental Sciences/Remote Sensing & Geospatial Sciences

description: The PhD in Economics program is designed to provide students with the training needed to carry out scholarly research in economics and to become professional economists in academia, government, or industry. Upon completion of the PhD, students will possess a thorough understanding of economic theory, applied economics, and quantitative methods. Doctoral students acquire research skills during their coursework and apply these skills in producing original research leading to a dissertation. Students completing the program are prepared to conduct research and teach in their field.
Program name: PhD in Economics

description: The Master of Science in Economic Policy & Practice (MS-EPP) is a new graduate program intended for students looking to develop an applied economics skillset and become leaders in the fields of economic policy and data analytics. Students will learn to analyze complex economic and social challenges using quantitative tools and communicate their findings effectively to a broad audience, with a view to shaping public policy. The program is specifically tailored to prepare students for careers in government agencies, international organizations, think tanks, consulting firms, and the private sector, where the ability to bridge economic theory with practical application is highly valued.
Program name: Master of Science in Economic Policy & Practice
Master of Science in Economics & Mathematics/Quantitative Economics

description: The MA in Global Development Economics (MA GDE) is a challenging one-year program that trains development practitioners in economic theory, quantitative methods, and policy analysis. The MA GDE is tailored for students who want to become leaders in development, whether in government, international organizations, NGOs, research centers, or the private sector. The program emphasizes economic modeling, econometrics, and program evaluation. The GDE program is STEM-designated and eligible for the STEM OPT extension.
Program name: Master of Arts in Global Development Economics

description: The Master of Arts in Quantitative Economics is a two-year program designed for students who want to develop strong analytical and quantitative skills for careers in finance, economics, business, and data science. The program helps students apply these skills to solve problems in these fields. The program also serves as a stepping stone for students who want to pursue a PhD in economics and other quantitatively oriented fields. The MA in Quantitative Economics is a STEM-designated program.
Program name: Master of Arts in Quantitative Economics

description: The MA in Editorial Studies offers intensive study in the history and theory of editing, and in the history of the book and print culture. Students acquire practical editorial experience through work on the papers of leading American literary figures, philosophers, and statesmen in the internationally known Boston University Stone Arch Initiatives. Students take courses both in the Editorial Institute and in relevant departments within the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. These courses typically focus on American literature, American history, and American studies, but may also include study of relevant European figures and movements. The program is excellent preparation for doctoral study in such fields as American literature, English literature, history, and American studies. Its unique combination of historical and practical work also qualifies graduates for positions in scholarly publishing.
Program name: Master of Arts in Editorial Studies

description: The Editorial Institute at Boston University is dedicated to editing and the history of the book. It offers an interdisciplinary PhD in Editorial Studies through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. Editorial Studies provides students with skills in textual scholarship and analytical bibliography, as well as an opportunity to gain experience in practical editing. Graduates are prepared for careers in higher education and other professions. The Institute welcomes inquiries from students in all fields of literary, historical, and philosophical study, especially those with a research interest in the theory and practice of scholarly editing.
Program name: PhD in Editorial Studies

description: The MA in English program prepares students for a variety of careers in academia, publishing, writing, and the arts, as well as for further study in a PhD program. The MA curriculum emphasizes depth and rigor across a broad range of Anglophone literatures and cultures, while giving students the opportunity to focus on particular areas of interest by selecting courses from a wide array of offerings across literary periods, genres, and theoretical approaches. Students gain experience in literary research, critical methodology, and written and oral communication, culminating in a final research paper or project.
Program name: Master of Arts in English

description: Boston University’s English MA program offers rigorous training in literary and cultural studies. Our curriculum covers the historical range of British and American literature while also fostering students’ engagement with various theoretical and methodological approaches and contemporary debates in the field. Students benefit from the program’s proximity to Boston’s rich literary history, its many cultural institutions, and its dynamic intellectual life. Our MA prepares students for PhD work, careers in secondary education, or further professional training in fields like law, business, and journalism.
Program name: Master of Arts / Juris Doctor in English

description: The PhD in English and American Literature prepares students for careers as scholars and teachers of literature, with an emphasis on research-intensive positions in higher education. Students develop their understanding of a wide range of literatures in English and critical theories, hone their skills as researchers and writers, and gain experience in the classroom through teaching opportunities in the Writing Program and the English Department. Students pursuing the PhD typically earn the MA in English and American Literature en route to the doctorate, which can be completed in five to six years. Our PhD is a fully funded program, which includes an annual stipend, a tuition scholarship, and a health insurance contribution. Students in the PhD program receive five years of funding, normally distributed as three years of Teaching Fellowship and two years of Scholarship or Fellowship.
Program name: PhD in English

description:
The MA Program in History is designed primarily to provide students with a solid grounding in the discipline of history while also allowing them to pursue their own areas of historical interest. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a number of professional careers as well as for further graduate study at the PhD level.

Program Learning Outcomes
*   Demonstrate knowledge of historical debates and historiographical traditions, especially within their fields of specialization.
*   Formulate a historical problem and develop an original argument, supported by evidence, in the form of a research paper or essay.
*   Carry out historical research, using both primary and secondary sources.
*   Communicate historical arguments clearly and effectively in both written and oral form.
*   Acquire professional skills appropriate for historians working in a variety of settings.
Program name: Master of Arts in History
PhD in History

description: The MA Program in the History of Art & Architecture at Boston University provides students with a broad and deep foundation in the methods, theories, and history of art and architectural history, while also allowing for specialization based on a student’s interests. Graduates of the program are prepared for doctoral work in art and architectural history, for museum work, and for a variety of professions that benefit from training in visual analysis, critical thinking, research, and writing. The program emphasizes both breadth and depth in students’ training. They take introductory courses in theory and methods, and also choose courses across different chronological periods and geographical areas from our diverse faculty. While the coursework ensures that students gain knowledge of a wide range of fields, students also select a major and minor field of specialization for their comprehensive exams and master’s thesis. The mission of Boston University’s MA Program in the History of Art & Architecture is to train students in the methods and theories of art and architectural history, provide them with a broad understanding of the field, and support their development of specialized knowledge in preparation for a range of professional futures, including doctoral study, museum work, and other careers requiring advanced skills in visual analysis, critical thinking, research, and writing. Upon completion of the program, students will: Demonstrate knowledge of the methods, theories, and historiography of art and architectural history; Develop specialized knowledge of at least two fields within art and architectural history and their respective scholarly traditions; Formulate an original research project based on a critical engagement with existing scholarship and primary sources; Present research effectively in written and oral forms; Teach confidently and effectively at the college level.
Program name: Master of Arts in History of Art & Architecture

description: Students may pursue a dual degree in law and the history of art and architecture, in conjunction with the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. The MA/JD in History of Art & Architecture prepares students to work with public and private collections, museums, and institutions involved in the law of art, cultural heritage, and historic preservation. The program is designed for completion within four years.
Program name: Master of Arts / Juris Doctor in History of Art & Architecture

description:
The Ph.D. program in the History of Art & Architecture is a highly selective and rigorous course of study designed to prepare students for careers as scholars and teachers of art and architectural history. We offer a comprehensive curriculum, with courses in areas ranging from ancient to contemporary art, and from the history of architecture to the history of photography. Through our program, students develop a mastery of art history, hone their research skills, deepen their understanding of theory and methodology, gain significant teaching experience, and participate in a vibrant intellectual community of faculty and students. In all these ways, our Ph.D. program prepares students to enter the profession with confidence and to make significant contributions to the field.

The department’s Ph.D. program is distinguished by its intimate size, encouraging close mentorship of students by faculty. Small classes and regular opportunities for informal exchange foster a strong sense of intellectual community. Our students are deeply involved in the life of the department, contributing to our speaker series and conferences, as well as to our undergraduate journal, Lux. The faculty is a community of outstanding scholars and award-winning teachers whose work spans a wide range of fields, methodologies, and critical approaches to the history of art and architecture. Our faculty members have active research programs in various fields including ancient, medieval, renaissance, baroque, eighteenth- and nineteenth-century European, American, Latin American, East Asian, and modern and contemporary art and architecture, as well as the history of photography.

All of our Ph.D. students are fully funded for five years, with an annual stipend and full tuition remission. Students also receive excellent training and experience as university teachers, typically beginning in their second year. During their second through fourth years, students gain valuable pedagogical experience by teaching sections of our large introductory lecture courses, with oversight and mentoring by the faculty member of record. Advanced doctoral students, after passing their qualifying exams, may also have the opportunity to teach their own introductory courses.

We encourage prospective applicants to contact faculty members whose research interests align with their own.
Program name: PhD in History of Art & Architecture

description: Boston University’s accelerated Mid-Career Master of Arts (MA) in International Relations program provides a robust, immersive, and intellectually rigorous curriculum for working professionals and individuals with substantial career experience. The MA in International Relations Mid-Career is designed for students seeking to advance existing careers, change career trajectories, or deepen their understanding of international affairs. This distinctive degree is completed in one academic year and prepares students for a diverse range of careers in diplomacy, government, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector.
Program name: Master of Arts in International Relations

description: The Pardee School PhD program in International Relations provides a small number of exceptional students with a rigorous, interdisciplinary, and policy-relevant education appropriate for careers as scholars and practitioners in international affairs. The program is designed to develop students’ analytic, research, and communication skills through a flexible curriculum that enables them to conduct original, cutting-edge research and successfully launch their careers in academia, government, or the private sector. Upon completion of the PhD in International Relations, students will be able to: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of major theories, issues, and research methods in international relations; Conduct original, independent research that contributes to scholarship in international relations; Clearly and effectively communicate research findings, both orally and in writing, to scholarly and policy audiences.
Program name: PhD in International Relations

description: The MA in Latin American Studies (M.A.L.A.S.) is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of Latin America. Students are able to combine courses in the humanities and social sciences across BU departments to pursue their interests in the politics, history, societies, and cultures of Latin America. The MA program provides excellent preparation for further graduate study in a doctoral program or for a career in government, NGOs, international organizations, journalism, or business.
Program name: Master of Arts in Latin American Studies

description: Students who pursue a PhD in Latin American Studies apply to, and are admitted by, one of Boston University’s disciplinary departments (e.g., Anthropology, History, Modern Languages and Comparative Literature, Political Science, Sociology). Students in the PhD program focus their disciplinary research on Latin America and complete the requirements for the PhD in Latin American Studies in addition to the requirements of their disciplinary department. Admission to the PhD program is highly competitive; therefore, applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic performance at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. All PhD students are fully funded, normally for five years, through a combination of stipends and tuition scholarships. For more information, please contact LAS. A full description of the requirements can be found in the Graduate Guide.
Program name: PhD in Latin American Studies

description: The MA in Linguistics is a two-year course of study leading to a thesis. It is designed to prepare students for doctoral study, and for careers requiring expertise in linguistics. The program offers comprehensive training in linguistic theory, research methods, and descriptive linguistics, with a strong emphasis on computational and experimental linguistics. Students develop a deep understanding of the structure and function of language, and gain hands-on experience in research and analysis. Graduates are well-prepared for PhD programs in linguistics or related fields, as well as positions in industry and government that require strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Program name: Master of Arts in Linguistics

description: The Department of Linguistics offers a PhD program in Linguistics. The goal of the PhD program is to provide students with a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistics and to prepare them to conduct independent research in the field. We offer courses and research opportunities in all of the main theoretical areas of linguistics, including phonology, phonetics, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics, as well as in areas such as psycholinguistics, computational linguistics, historical linguistics, field methods, and language acquisition. Our students are trained to develop their own original research programs and to contribute to the advancement of linguistic theory. They also have opportunities to gain experience in teaching and to participate in interdisciplinary research projects. Most students admitted to the PhD program receive five years of funding, covering tuition and health insurance, plus a stipend in return for teaching duties and/or research assistantships. Exceptional students may be considered for merit fellowships which do not have teaching or research requirements. Students complete coursework and examinations in the core areas of linguistics, conduct original research, and write a dissertation. The program culminates in the defense of the dissertation. Students typically complete the program in 5–6 years. For more information about specific program requirements, see the GRS Bulletin.
Program name: PhD in Linguistics

description: The Master of Fine Arts (MFA) in Literary Translation is a two-year, 48-credit program based in the Editorial Institute. It offers an intensive course of study in literary translation for students who aim to develop their skills and knowledge as professional translators. The program combines academic training in translation theory and history with practical experience in various genres and styles. Students work closely with faculty mentors, many of whom are accomplished translators and scholars, and engage with a vibrant community of writers and translators in Boston and beyond. The MFA program in Literary Translation provides a rigorous curriculum designed to cultivate highly skilled and reflective translators. Students delve into the nuances of language, culture, and literary style, gaining expertise in translating poetry, prose, and drama. The program emphasizes a hands-on approach, with workshops focused on practical translation techniques, editing, and revision. In addition to core translation courses, students explore relevant fields such as comparative literature, linguistics, and publishing. The curriculum culminates in a substantial translation project, often publishable quality, accompanied by a critical introduction.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Literary Translation

description: Offered by the Department of Literatures in English and Romance Studies, the MFA in Literary Translation at Boston University is a two-year, full-time program. The MFA program in Literary Translation provides a rigorous curriculum in literary translation and translation studies, leading to the completion of a book-length translation into English from one of many source languages. Students may specialize in translation from a range of languages into English, including Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Latin, Modern Greek, Polish, Russian, and Spanish. The program is designed for students interested in careers as literary translators, editors, and scholars. It is ideally suited for those seeking to combine the practical application of translating with the study of translation theory and history.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Chinese/Literary Translation

description: The MFA in Literary Translation is a terminal degree that provides an intensive course of study in translation practice, theory, and history. Students in the MFA program receive training in comparative literary studies while developing their skills as literary translators. The MFA requires a total of 32 credits (eight courses) and a translation thesis submitted in the final semester. Students generally complete the program in two years. With faculty guidance, students develop their individual interests and create a translation portfolio and a substantial thesis, often of publishable quality. They emerge from the program prepared for a career as a professional translator, or for further graduate study in comparative literature, literary translation, or a related field. The MFA degree is housed in the Department of Comparative Literature.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Comparative Literature/Literary Translation

description: The MFA in Literary Translation is a two-year program for students of exceptional linguistic and literary talent. The program is designed to provide students with thorough training in the practice of literary translation as well as a solid grounding in translation studies, literary history and theory, and comparative literature. Students are expected to complete a thesis consisting of a book-length literary translation accompanied by an introduction and footnotes. The program has a strong international focus and includes a number of opportunities for students to study abroad, including a summer course in Venice, Italy, and exchange programs with universities in Geneva, Switzerland; Leuven, Belgium; and Shanghai, China.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in French Studies/Literary Translation

description: The Boston University Master of Fine Arts (MFA) in Literary Translation is a two-year, 48-credit program that includes study in the theory and practice of literary translation, as well as the translation of literary texts from a foreign language into English. Students may specialize in Chinese, French, German, Japanese, and Spanish. Graduates are prepared for careers as literary translators, editors, and publishers, as well as for further study in a PhD program. The program provides an opportunity for students to refine their own work through workshops; to participate in the translation community through various conferences, talks, and campus visits by writers and translators; to gain experience in literary publishing; and to develop their own critical and historical understanding of the art of translation.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in German/Literary Translation

description: Our MFA program in Literary Translation provides a rigorous professional training in the theory and practice of literary translation in several languages, primarily from French, German, Italian, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese, and Japanese. The program emphasizes an informed, critical approach to literary translation, grounded in a close reading of texts and an understanding of the cultural and historical contexts in which they arise. Working closely with active literary translators, students develop professional skills through hands-on practice, translation workshops, translation theory courses, and directed individual studies that culminate in the production of a book-length translation and the professional portfolio required for entry into the field. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers as literary translators, editors, and scholars, and for further doctoral work in comparative literature or related fields.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Japanese/Literary Translation

description: The BA in Spanish + MFA in Literary Translation is a five-year program that prepares students for careers in translation while offering a firm grounding in the liberal arts. The program provides the linguistic, cultural, and literary knowledge essential for high-level work in literary translation. Through coursework and supervised practice, students hone the analytical skills required to produce publishable translations in a variety of fields, from fiction and poetry to academic prose and commercial texts. The program is ideal for students with advanced Spanish language skills and a strong interest in literature and writing. Graduates of the program are well-prepared to pursue careers in publishing, international relations, education, and other fields that require advanced linguistic and intercultural competence.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Spanish/Literary Translation

description: The MA in Mathematics & Statistics is intended for students who want to strengthen their mathematical background and prepare for a PhD in mathematics or statistics, or for those who wish to pursue a career that involves significant mathematical or statistical knowledge. The program offers flexibility, allowing students to tailor their courses to fit their individual interests and career goals. Students choose courses from across a wide range of fields in mathematics and statistics, including pure and applied mathematics, probability, mathematical statistics, computational statistics, and data science. The program can be completed in two to four semesters of full-time study.
Program name: Master of Arts in Mathematics & Statistics

description: The Department of Mathematics & Statistics at Boston University offers the PhD in Mathematics & Statistics. Our doctoral program is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of advanced mathematical and statistical concepts, as well as the research skills necessary to contribute new knowledge to the field. Through rigorous coursework, comprehensive exams, and original dissertation research, students prepare for careers in academia, industry, and government. Our faculty are active researchers in a wide range of mathematical and statistical disciplines, providing students with diverse opportunities for mentorship and collaboration. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, encouraging students to engage with real-world problems. We strive to develop independent scholars capable of critical thinking, problem-solving, and effective communication of complex ideas.
Program name: PhD in Mathematics & Statistics

description: The MA in Mathematics program is intended for students with a strong background in mathematics who wish to deepen their mathematical knowledge and pursue further study in mathematics or a related field, or to pursue a career in teaching or in a field requiring advanced mathematical skills. Students completing the MA in Mathematics program will have a solid foundation in the core areas of analysis and algebra and will have the opportunity to take advanced courses in a variety of other areas of mathematics. The MA program provides an excellent background for students considering doctoral studies in mathematics. The program can be completed in one or two years depending on the student’s background and course load.
Program name: Master of Science in Mathematics

description: The Master of Science in Statistical Practice (MSSP) program is designed to provide students with the statistical skills necessary for success in business, government, and not-for-profit organizations. The program focuses on the effective application of statistical methods to the acquisition and analysis of data. It also emphasizes communication skills for conveying statistical ideas, models, and results to non-statistical audiences. Graduates are prepared for careers as practicing statisticians in industries such as finance, marketing, pharmaceutical, information technology, and government.
Program name: Master of Science in Statistical Practice

description: The MA in Statistics program provides advanced training in statistical methods and theory, along with important computational skills. The program is designed for students with strong quantitative backgrounds who wish to acquire a sophisticated understanding of statistics in preparation for either a career as a practicing statistician or for further graduate study in statistics or a related field. Students will learn how to apply powerful statistical methods to solve real-world problems. The program emphasizes the modern approach to statistics, which is data driven and heavily reliant on computation. The MA program provides a solid foundation in the theory and application of statistics and prepares students to analyze data in a wide range of fields, including bioinformatics, economics, education, engineering, environmental science, finance, public health, and social sciences. Full-time students complete the MA program in one academic year (two semesters). Part-time students may complete the program in two years.
Program name: Master of Arts in Statistics

description: The PhD in Statistics program at Boston University’s Graduate School of Arts & Sciences provides students with a strong foundation in both classical and modern statistical theory and methodology, as well as computational statistics, statistical machine learning, and data science. The program trains students for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they will conduct novel theoretical and methodological research, develop new statistical methods, and apply statistical principles to real-world problems. We welcome applicants with a strong background in mathematics and an interest in probability and statistics. Our program emphasizes flexibility, allowing students to tailor their coursework and research to their specific interests and career goals. Students work closely with faculty mentors on cutting-edge research projects, gaining hands-on experience in data analysis, statistical modeling, and scientific communication. As a student in the PhD in Statistics program, you will: Develop a deep understanding of statistical theory and methodology. Gain expertise in computational statistics and data science. Learn to conduct independent research and contribute to the field of statistics. Collaborate with faculty on innovative research projects. Prepare for a successful career in academia, industry, or government.
Program name: PhD in Statistics

description: The Department of Biology offers an MA program in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry. This program provides students with advanced training in these fields through coursework and participation in a research laboratory. The program is specifically designed to prepare students for a career in biotechnology or for further graduate study toward a PhD. The department houses research groups with interests in molecular genetics, structural biology, membrane biophysics, bacterial physiology, cellular neurobiology, signal transduction, tumor biology, immunology, virology, and developmental biology. These laboratories employ a wide range of state-of-the-art methodologies. Students have the opportunity to select an area of research that matches their interests. All students participate in the weekly seminar series and several journal clubs. Students also acquire teaching experience by serving as teaching fellows in a laboratory course.
Program name: Master of Arts in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry

description: The Department of Biology, Department of Chemistry, and Department of Medical Sciences & Education offer an interdisciplinary PhD in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry. Students choose to specialize in one of these three participating departments or may pursue a truly interdisciplinary research program involving two or more of the participating departments. Students are prepared for careers in academia, biotechnology, and other scientific fields.
Program name: PhD in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry

description: The MA in Musicology program is intended both for students who wish to pursue a doctorate in musicology or in an allied field, and for those who wish to enhance their professional capabilities (e.g., in teaching, librarianship, arts administration, or other careers for which advanced training in the critical and historical study of music is an asset). The program cultivates advanced skills in writing, critical thinking, research, and analysis of topics in musicology. Students take courses in musicological methods, bibliography, and a broad range of subjects in music history. The MA in Musicology program is part of the Department of Musicology & Ethnomusicology within the School of Music, College of Fine Arts. Visit the department website for more information.
Program name: Master of Arts in Musicology

description: Boston University offers PhDs in ethnomusicology, musicology, and music theory and composition. With small, intimate programs, students receive extensive individual attention and benefit from a wide variety of coursework within the School of Music, the Department of Musicology and Ethnomusicology, and the broader university. Doctoral students are fully funded for five years with tuition, health insurance, and a stipend. Many of our students teach in the undergraduate core curriculum, receive teaching certificates from BU’s Center for Teaching & Learning, and go on to tenure-track jobs. The PhD in Musicology at BU is designed to train independent scholars for careers in teaching and research, and to provide comprehensive grounding in all areas of historical musicology. Graduates have gone on to prestigious positions in academia and related fields.
Program name: PhD in Musicology

description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Neuroscience program is designed for students who desire a deeper understanding of the field and wish to enhance their academic credentials. The MA in Neuroscience can serve as a stepping stone for students interested in pursuing a PhD, or those who wish to build a strong foundation for a career in research or health-related professions. The MA program provides a broad foundation in neuroscience through core coursework and mentored research experiences in the laboratories of faculty who are members of the Graduate Program for Neuroscience (GPN). Students complete either a thesis (Plan A) or a non-thesis (Plan B) option depending on their interests and goals, with the thesis option providing more intensive research experience. Both plans require a minimum of 32 graduate credits.
Program name: Master of Arts in Neuroscience

description: The Graduate Program for Neuroscience (GPN) is an interdisciplinary PhD program based at the Boston University Charles River and Medical Campuses. Students in the GPN benefit from the breadth of neuroscience expertise across Boston University as they train in the field with faculty from multiple departments. Faculty research interests span the full spectrum of neuroscience, from molecules to mind and from discovery to clinical application. Students in the GPN are exposed to diverse research opportunities, a flexible curriculum, and numerous chances for professional development that prepare them for a variety of careers in neuroscience. Students completing the program are equipped to pursue careers in academia, industry, and related fields.
Program name: PhD in Neuroscience

description: Boston University’s Master of Arts in Global Policy (MAGP) program, offered jointly by the Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies and the Department of Political Science, addresses the growing demand for professionals who can understand and critically engage with complex global challenges. The program aims to educate students to become leaders who can apply theory to policy in an interdisciplinary way. Graduates will be equipped with critical thinking, analytical, and professional skills required to address global challenges in areas such as international security, international development, human rights, and diplomacy. Through a rigorous curriculum and practical experience, students will gain expertise in policymaking, policy analysis, and program evaluation within an international context. This program provides students with a strong foundation in global policy and prepares them for careers in international organizations, government agencies, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector.
Program name: Master of Arts in Global Policy

Concentration name: Diplomacy, Global Economic Affairs, Religion and International Affairs
description: The MA in International Affairs is the Pardee School of Global Studies’ flagship graduate program, designed for students interested in careers in international service and global affairs. Our program is distinctive for combining the interdisciplinary study of global issues with professional training in policymaking. Our curriculum offers students the opportunity to learn from the Pardee School’s diverse faculty of scholars and practitioners. The program’s core curriculum emphasizes the study of analytical tools and frameworks for understanding international affairs. It also offers students the opportunity to develop and hone a wide range of analytical skills, including quantitative, qualitative, and historical methods. The Pardee School of Global Studies has a strong commitment to practical application and professional training. We provide numerous opportunities for students to apply their knowledge and skills in real-world settings through internships, practicums, and research projects. Our program prepares students for careers in government, non-governmental organizations, international organizations, and the private sector. Pardee School students are uniquely poised to address the most pressing global challenges of the 21st century. The MA program provides graduates with the analytical tools, professional skills, and global experience necessary to tackle these challenges effectively.
Program name: Master of Arts in International Affairs

description: The MA/MBA combined degree program at Boston University offers students the opportunity to combine a Master of Arts in International Relations with a Master of Business Administration. Offered jointly by the Pardee School of Global Studies and the Questrom School of Business, this program offers students an interdisciplinary education at the intersection of international affairs and management. Designed to be completed in two years, the MA/MBA program prepares students for careers in the private, public, and nonprofit sectors, working with multinational corporations, international financial institutions, or international organizations.
Program name: Master of Arts in International Relations / Master of Business Administration

description: The JD/MA in International Relations offers students the opportunity to combine the study of law with the study of international relations. Both degrees emphasize a critical and interdisciplinary approach to their subject matter.
